title: Mobilization and Service Commencement Terms of the Workplace Cafe Management Program
content:
A Workplace Cafe Management Program contract is opened as a proposal, moves into mobilization on countersignature, and only opens to employees once the opening project is complete. The opening project fee, the refundable equipment deposit and the opening inventory investment are those printed against the service model proposed, and the opening project fee is invoiced when mobilization starts rather than at commencement.

**Working the contract during mobilization.** A contract may only be worked on for mobilization while it stands proposed, mobilizing or active. A proposal that is withdrawn before countersignature closes without any opening project fee falling due — this is read from the contract's own status on record, taken before the mobilization work is carried out, for that contract alone.

**The lead time before service can start.** Service may not commence earlier than the mobilisation lead time printed against the service model, counted in calendar days from the day the client countersigns the cafe management contract. Calendar days are counted from the day after countersignature, every day of the week counts, and the boundary day itself is a permitted commencement day; calendar days are never converted into full 24-hour periods. The clock is read off the countersignature date recorded against the contract.

Suppose, purely as a hypothetical, a contract is countersigned on the 3rd of March and the mobilisation lead time printed against its service model is, hypothetically, 10 calendar days: counting from the 4th of March, the day after countersignature, the 10th calendar day reached is the 13th of March, so the 13th of March is a commencement day that just satisfies the lead time, while the 12th of March, one day short of it, just fails to satisfy it.

Where the client asks to open earlier than the lead time allows, the opening is not accelerated: the request is declined and the earliest permitted commencement day is offered instead. Where the entry gate for the proposed service model is not met by the site's reported headcount or annual food spend, the proposal is written instead for the highest service model whose entry gate the site does meet.
